thesis: This episode argues that Walmart is the dominant force in American retail, specifically having successfully 'nailed' the grocery category to become the largest grocer by the end of the 1990s. It contrasts Walmart's massive scale and profitability in groceries against the struggles of Amazon to crack the same category and the historical decline of Kmart.

claims.claim: Walmart is the largest retailer in America and the largest grocery store in the United States today.
claims.quote: By 1990, Walmart passed Sears to become the largest retailer in America. All through the '70s and the '80s Kmart was the gorilla. And then by the early '90s, Kmart, which had been so dominant, started really feeling the squeeze from Walmart because Walmart is now pretty much nationwide at this point.

claims.claim: Walmart is the largest grocery store in the United States today by a factor of over 2X the number 2 player.
claims.quote: David: Now, they are not just the largest grocery store, they are the largest grocery store by a factor of over 2X the number 2 player. Ben: Which is Kroger. Who's two? David: Kroger, yup.

claims.quote: Ben: Walmart has over 20% market share of US groceries, Kroger has under 10% and then Albertsons and Costco are tied at 5% each.

claims.claim: Walmart nailed the grocery category, becoming the largest grocer in America by the end of the '90s.
claims.quote: Walmart went from 0% market share in US grocery at the beginning of the '90s to by the end of the decade in the '90s, they had become the largest grocer in America.

claims.claim: Grocery items in a Walmart Supercenter are 15% cheaper than a comparable grocery store on average.
claims.quote: Most items, by and large on average across the board, the grocery items in a Walmart Supercenter are 15% cheaper than a comparable grocery store.
